attributes.residual: UNCHANGED from the superseding v2: real 497, insns T843/O844, opcode multiset 1t with TARGET-ONLY EMPTY, one genuine structural row - a single surplus `fmr` in the FIRST clamp group only, at +0x5e8..+0x600. Re-derived live this run rather than quoted: ours emits `fcmpo f6,f1 / bge / fmr f0,f1 / b / fcmpo f6,f5 / ble / fmr f0,f5 / b / fmr f0,f6 / stfs f0` where the target emits `fcmpo f1,f5 / bge / b / fcmpo f1,f0 / ble / b / fmr f0,f1 / fmr f5,f0 / stfs f5`. THE MEASUREMENT THIS RUN ADDS, and it sharpens the law's mechanism: the target holds STABLE function-wide FPR homes across the clamp groups (lo=f5, hi=f0, sc=f4 in BOTH group 1 and group 2), whereas OUR build gives lo and hi DIFFERENT homes per group (group 1 lo=f1, hi=f5, sc=f0; group 2 lo=f5, hi=f6, sc=f0). So the surplus word is not a property of the first group's spelling at all - it is that our lo/hi live ranges are split and coloured per group, and in group 1 the ternary's result therefore lands in a scratch f0 (freed when sc dies) rather than in lo's home, which makes BOTH identity arms non-empty. Groups 2-5 reproduce the target byte-shape exactly. Also re-confirmed live: group 1 and group 2 are character-for-character identical in source shape apart from their pif indices and p_parms index, which is independent confirmation of the law's finding that the defect is allocator-side and not spelling-side. The one carrier the law names for a cure - giving the destination an earlier definition in the SAME scope - has no zero-cost site here: lines 2076-2117 of the function contain no scale/clamp triple and no other consumer of sc/lo/hi, so any earlier definition would have to be invented and would cost instructions. NOT WEBFRANK-ELIGIBLE, unchanged: a surplus INSTRUCTION is not a register field and the postprocessor cannot delete a word.

denial.falsifier: Any declaration-site edit to sc/lo/hi that changes setWorldParms's object bytes in the +0x5e8..+0x600 window - that alone would disprove the premise that declaration-site spelling does not reach this decision. More strongly: a build in which lo and hi hold one stable FPR home across all five clamp groups, however obtained, would disprove the claim that the per-group live-range split is not source-controllable here.
denial.premise_measurement: Seven probes across two runs, all leaving the single genuine structural row untouched, and three of them NEUTRAL-IDENTICAL at the object-byte level: declaration order `f32 lo, hi, sc;` byte-identical; `#pragma opt_lifetimes on` byte-identical; `register f32 sc, lo, hi;` byte-identical (measured this run, real held at 497, T843/O844, 1t). The four non-identical ones all regressed or held structure: declared before t0..t3 real 497 -> 501; assignment into the inner else arm real 557; comma-operator form real 637 with insns 848 and multiset 5t; `opt_lifetimes off` insns 847 multiset 6t. Three byte-identical results mean the source text is not reaching the compiler's decision point, which is why the class is closed rather than merely unlucky.

hypothesis.cheapest_refuting_observation: Read the FPR homes of lo and hi in all five clamp groups of the TARGET. If the target's homes are NOT stable across all five - if it too re-colours per group and merely happens to pick lo's home in group 1 - then there is no stable-home property to reproduce and this framing is wrong; the word would then be an ordinary colouring accident with no source carrier at all.
hypothesis.screened_against_target: yes - FPR homes read from the aligned view in two different groups of the same function. Target: lo=f5, hi=f0, sc=f4 in group 1 AND group 2. Ours: group 1 lo=f1, hi=f5, sc=f0; group 2 lo=f5, hi=f6, sc=f0. Groups 2-5 already reproduce the target byte-shape, so only group 1's colouring is wrong, and the source of groups 1 and 2 is character-for-character identical apart from indices.
hypothesis.statement: Attack the twins' surplus fmr as a LIVE-RANGE problem rather than a declaration or spelling problem: find a source form that makes lo and hi hold ONE stable FPR home across all five clamp groups, as the target does, instead of being re-coloured per group. The per-group split is the measured root cause - in group 1 it leaves the ternary's result in a scratch FPR (sc's home, freed by the multiply) instead of lo's home, which is what makes both identity arms non-empty and costs the word.
